_README: Executable half of .claude/DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md. The markdown holds the
narrative; this holds the one thing prose cannot do — answer 'is it still
broken?' by being RUN.
WHY: on 2026-08-12 the tracker said DQ-54 was 'Open — report-only' when it
had been fixed and merged that morning, and its own row said 'three call
sites' when there were nine. Its header said Last Updated 2026-08-08. A
hand-written status decays silently, and this repo has the receipts: #398
hid for ten weeks, DQ-54's prose recurred in four days.
THE RATCHET RUNS BOTH WAYS — that is the whole point:
declared 'fixed' + check FAILS  -> red. A regression, or a fix that never was.
declared 'open'  + check PASSES -> red. Silently fixed; the ledger is lying
the other way and nobody would ever look.
Only the second direction catches the failure mode that actually hurt here.
COVERAGE: every DQ id in the markdown must appear here. A new row without an
entry fails the coverage test, so the ledger cannot grow un-checkable rows.
Same shape as scripts/check_test_quarantine.py, which already works this way.
check: null is HONEST, not a TODO to hide behind. It means nobody has written
a falsifiable check yet, and the count of nulls is reported on every run so
the gap stays visible. An invented check that cannot fail is what produced
DQ-30's '0% drift' verification — worse than no check.

DQ-32.note: Fixed 2026-08-13 under the present-all ruling. ⚠ The old probe counted 562 rows in ambiguous groups and treated every one as a defect; 556 of them already state their case and are correct. Counting those is what made this look like weeks of adjudication when the real defect was a component dropping a field the API already sent. The remaining 6 conditionless rows are DQ-32c. This check is a jest test because the defect was in RENDERING - a DB probe cannot see it, which is exactly why it survived so long. The check needs frontend-nextjs/node_modules, so it runs in CI's Jest job (both runtimes) and reports UNVERIFIED anywhere they are absent rather than failing.

The right shape is a stored url_page_last_status column written by the existing monitor, then a probe that counts non-200s. That column does not exist yet.

DQ-62.passes_when: exit 0 - no stored commencement postdates its own plan's name by 3+ years
DQ-62.red_when: A stored commencement is an amendment or consolidation date, which decides WHICH plan governs an application and so cannot be approximated.
DQ-62.note: Scope corrected 2026-08-13: this was recorded as parramatta-only and it is systemic. scan_statement returned max(effective dates), so wherever a document printed both its commencement and a later amendment the amendment won - the exact inversion of DQ-60. Four more councils carry the result: strathfield (DCP 2005 -> 2020-09-08), burwood (2013 -> 2026-03-05), fairfield (2013 -> 2024-08-22), the_hills (2012 -> 2022-05-06). WRITER FIXED: it now takes the earliest, returns None when the spread is 3+ years rather than guessing, and amendment tables write currency_* instead. The four stored values predate the fix and each needs its real commencement located; clearing them would raise the count the as-at ratchet guards.

DQ-66.passes_when: exit 0 - no control is served council-wide while citing a plan that covers one town
DQ-66.red_when: A control is served to a whole council area citing a plan that governs one town, because sibling town plans are registered with nothing extracted from them.
DQ-66.note: CLAIM CORRECTED 2026-08-13. The row said 'A Mittagong or Moss Vale property is being given Bowral's setbacks' - implying wrong numbers. It is not: all three town plans were downloaded and hash-matched to dcp_chapter_registry.content_hash, and Part C Sections 2-4, which back all 32 stored controls, are NUMERICALLY IDENTICAL across them (100/40/16 numeric tokens per section, zero differences in all six pairwise comparisons). The defect is MIS-CITATION - the reference names a plan that does not govern the property, and table numbering differs between plans, so it does not resolve. The 'known to maintain several plans' half that was said to have no data behind it does: the registry lists all three town plans, all is_active. Separate and larger gap recorded as DQ-67: Part C Sections 16+ are town-specific precincts, entirely different per plan, and none are extracted for any town. OPEN DECISION on how this reaches zero: extracting Mittagong and Moss Vale would create ~60 rows duplicating values already proven identical, which is not obviously an improvement. The alternative is to re-cite these 30 to the common Part C of Wingecarribee DCP 2010 rather than to one town's plan. The probe measures the state, not the preferred remedy.

DQ-67.why_no_check: Found while correcting DQ-66 on 2026-08-13. Wingecarribee's three town plans share Part C Sections 1-15 verbatim but diverge completely from Section 16 on, where the town-specific precincts live - Bowral has 9 (Bowral Conservation, Shepherd Street, OLSH, Retford Park and more), Mittagong 5 (Central Heritage, The Maltings, Renwick, Mount Gibraltar), Moss Vale 7 (Railway Street, Elizabeth Street North and South, Kirkham Street). None are extracted for ANY town, including Bowral. These are where the genuinely different numbers are, so this is the larger half of what DQ-66 was pointing at. A count needs a per-plan inventory of which sections carry numeric controls, which does not exist - counting registry chapters with no extracted controls would conflate a non-residential chapter with an unextracted one and return hundreds.
